source.title: Champions League tactical insights: Cucurella excels — clip 1 (Chelsea counterpressing)

situation.outcome: Malo Gusto's challenge helps Chelsea regain and progress forward quickly
situation.human_observation: This is the opening clip of the first video in the article, illustrating Chelsea's collective intensity via counterpressing during their 3-0 win over Barcelona. Per the article: this was a team who, on losing the ball, worked aggressively to win it back, as seen with Malo Gusto's challenge to regain the ball — and once they had it back, they were quick and direct in progressing it forward. The article notes this intensity is a recurring theme for Chelsea under manager Enzo Maresca, also referencing a similar pattern in a prior UEFA Conference League final analysis against Real Betis.
situation.priority_problem: How to react immediately and aggressively upon losing the ball (rather than retreating passively), win it back through a committed individual challenge, and then transition quickly into direct forward progression rather than resetting into a slower buildup.
visible_evidence: Chelsea lose possession in the middle/attacking third.
Players react immediately and aggressively to try to win the ball back rather than dropping off.
Malo Gusto makes the challenge that regains possession for Chelsea.
Following the regain, Chelsea progress the ball quickly and directly, rather than resetting possession slowly.

coaching.objective: Develop the immediate, aggressive reaction needed to win the ball back quickly after losing it, and the decision-making to progress directly and quickly once possession is regained, rather than resetting into a slow buildup.
coaching.practice_design: Small-sided possession-to-transition practice: on a coached or random turnover, the team without the ball must press immediately and aggressively to win it back (rather than retreat), with a specific emphasis on committing to challenges (as Gusto does in this clip) rather than delaying or standing off. Once the ball is regained, reward/require quick, direct forward passes or dribbles rather than safe sideways/backward passes, reinforcing the 'regain and go' pattern. Time-pressure constraints (e.g. must play forward within 1-2 touches of winning the ball) can help ingrain the directness.
success_cues: Players closest to the ball react immediately and aggressively upon losing possession.
At least one player commits fully to a challenge to win the ball back, rather than jockeying passively.
The ball is regained through that committed challenge.
Immediately after the regain, the team progresses the ball quickly and directly upfield rather than resetting slowly.
